files.Title: Egap.Documents.Block
files.Summary: A node that goes into a story or a table cell: a paragraph or a table. Content controls and kept islands join in Build Plan task 5.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.BlockContainer
files.Summary: A node that holds blocks: a story (body, header, footer) or a table cell.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.BlockIsland
files.Summary: A block kept whole, such as an embedded document part (Word's altChunk), as raw markup.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Body
files.Summary: A section's main text.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Bookmark
files.Summary: A bookmark found in a document: its start, its end if any, and the text between.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.BookmarkEnd
files.Summary: The end of a bookmark range.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.BookmarkStart
files.Summary: The start of a bookmark: a named place, or a named range up to the of the same name.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Border
files.Summary: One border line: style, width and colour, the space between it and the text, and Word's shadow and frame flags.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.BorderStyle
files.Summary: A line style for borders, as Word's border types without the art borders (kept by the DOCX reader as extension data).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.BoxCorners
files.Summary: The radius of each corner of a box, in points; 0 for a square corner.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.BoxShadow
files.Summary: A shadow a box casts (CSS box-shadow): the box's shape moved by the offsets, grown by and blurred by , drawn behind the box.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.BoxStyle
files.Summary: How a box is drawn around its content: margins, padding, borders, background, rounded corners and a shadow, and the size it asks for. Flex and grid containers and their items, and groups of blocks (), take one. Immutable; set a new one to change the box.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Break
files.Summary: A line, page or column break inside a paragraph.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.BreakKind
files.Summary: What a ends.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.BuiltInStyle
files.Summary: Styles Word knows by name, which adds with Word 2013+'s definitions.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Cell
files.Summary: A table cell: blocks, nested tables included. Word wants at least one paragraph in every cell; the model allows none, and writers add the paragraph where the format needs it.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.CellFormat
files.Summary: Table cell formatting: width, merges, vertical alignment, margins, borders and shading. Every property is nullable: null means not set here.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.CharacterStyle
files.Summary: A character style: character formatting for runs.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Comment
files.Summary: A comment: its reference mark in the text, holding the comment's own text, author and date (Phase 6 design Q8). The text it is about lies between a and with its . A reply names the comment it answers in , as Word does.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.CommentRangeEnd
files.Summary: The end of the text a is about; it pairs with the comment by .

files.Title: Egap.Documents.CommentRangeStart
files.Summary: The start of the text a is about; it pairs with the comment by .

files.Title: Egap.Documents.CommentStory
files.Summary: The text of a comment.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.CompositeInline
files.Summary: An inline that holds other inlines: a hyperlink or an inline content control.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ContentControl
files.Summary: A content control around blocks: paragraphs, tables and other controls.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ContentControlKind
files.Summary: What kind of content control (Word's structured document tag) it is.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ContentControlProperties
files.Summary: The settings content controls have, block or inline: kind, tag, title, locks and placeholder state.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ControlChar
files.Summary: The characters uses for what is not text, as Word's own text ranges do.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ConversionWarning
files.Summary: One kind of thing a writer left out, with how many times it happened.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ConversionWarningKind
files.Summary: What a reader or writer had to leave out or change because a format cannot hold it.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DoclingImage
files.Summary: A picture's image for .

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DoclingImageMode
files.Summary: How writes pictures' images.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DoclingJson
files.Summary: Layout as DoclingDocument JSON (design Q14, Build Plan task 18), the format Docling writes, schema version : texts, tables, pictures and list groups in flat arrays, linked into reading order from the body by JSON pointers; roles as Docling's labels; bounds as provenance with the page number and a box from the page's bottom left, as PDF measures; page headers and footers in the furniture layer; and Egap's role and confidence in each item's meta. A DoclingDocument from Docling reads back into page layouts.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DoclingJsonOptions
files.Summary: How writes.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Document
files.Summary: A flow document: a list of sections, each with its page setup, body and headers and footers, holding paragraphs, tables and the rest of the model (Phase 6 design Q3). The root of the tree; every other node belongs to exactly one document.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocumentBuilder
files.Summary: Barcodes.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocumentChangeKind
files.Summary: What happened in a notification.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocumentChangedEventArgs
files.Summary: One change to a document (Phase 6 design Q3, editor-ready model): the node, what happened to it and where. Code that keeps a view of the document, such as another library's editor or a cache, redraws from these; undo and redo can be built on them too.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocumentColor
files.Summary: A colour as documents give it: automatic, a fixed colour, or a theme colour with Word's tint (towards white) or shade (towards black), so a theme change recolours the text that uses it. The default value is automatic.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocumentColorKind
files.Summary: How a is given.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocumentException
files.Summary: A file could not be read as the format it was given as: not a package, a part missing or malformed beyond repair.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocumentFormatKind
files.Summary: The kind of file finds, without loading it.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocumentLimitException
files.Summary: A file went past one of the reader's limits (Phase 6 design Q9: part sizes, entry counts, compression ratio, nesting), so reading stopped instead of using unbounded memory or time. The limits are in the format's load options.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocumentLimits
files.Summary: The limits a reader keeps to on untrusted files; the defaults suit any real document.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocumentPreview
files.Summary: Sends a document's pages to the egap-preview tool (dotnet tool install -g Egap.Preview), which shows them on a local web page and shows them again each time new pages arrive: run the code under dotnet watch and the page follows every edit.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocumentProperties
files.Summary: A document's properties: the core ones every format knows (title, author, dates) and custom ones by name, which fields such as TITLE, AUTHOR and DOCPROPERTY show.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocumentSettings
files.Summary: Document-wide settings that change layout and numbering: the default tab stop, odd and even headers, footnote and endnote numbering, change tracking and Word's compatibility mode. Word's other settings are kept by the DOCX reader as extension data on the document.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocumentVisitor
files.Summary: Walks a document tree through : a start and an end method for each node that holds others, one method for each inline. Override the ones you need; the rest continue. The walk does not recurse, so deeply nested tables cannot overflow the stack.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocxFormat
files.Summary: Word's DOCX format, with its DOTX and DOCM variants (Phase 6 design Q9 and Q10): strict and transitional files read into the model, with what the model does not name kept as extension data so a DOCX round trip keeps it.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocxKind
files.Summary: Which of Word's file kinds a DOCX package is (Phase 6 design Q10).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocxLoadOptions
files.Summary: How reads a file.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.DocxSaveOptions
files.Summary: How writes a file.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.EmbeddedFont
files.Summary: A font file a document carries (Phase 6 design Q10 and Q12): the layout engine looks here first for a family's face.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ExtensionData
files.Summary: What a format's reader found on a node that the model does not name, kept so the same format's writer can put it back (Phase 6 design Q7): for DOCX, unknown elements and attributes as raw XML with their place among the mapped children. Each format keeps its own data under its name ("docx", "html"); writers of other formats leave it alone. An edit that removes a node removes its data with it.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Field
files.Summary: A field as a whole: its start, separator and end and the nodes between them. The code is the text between the start and the separator (or the end); the result is between the separator and the end. Fields nest, as in Word.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.FieldEnd
files.Summary: The end of a field (Word's fldChar end).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.FieldKind
files.Summary: The kind of a field, from the first word of its code. Fields Egap does not know are and keep their stored result (Phase 6 design Q8).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.FieldSeparator
files.Summary: The separator between a field's code and its result (Word's fldChar separate).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.FieldStart
files.Summary: The start of a field (Word's fldChar begin). A field is a start, its code (runs), an optional separator, its result (runs, maybe over several paragraphs) and an end; gathers them.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.FindOptions
files.Summary: How and match.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.FlexContainer
files.Summary: A flex container (CSS flexbox): items laid out in a row or a column, growing and shrinking to share the space, wrapped onto more lines when they ask for it. The page flow breaks between lines; DOCX writes the container as a borderless table.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.FlexDirection
files.Summary: Which way a flex container lays its items out.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.FlexItem
files.Summary: An item of a : blocks laid out in a box that grows and shrinks with the line.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.FlexLayout
files.Summary: How a flex container lays out its items (CSS flexbox): direction, wrapping, how the space left on a line is shared and how items line up across it, and the gaps between items and lines. Immutable; set a new one to change it.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.FlexWrap
files.Summary: Whether a flex container's items go on more lines when they do not fit on one.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.FloatingAlignment
files.Summary: Where a floating object lines up within what it is measured from, instead of an offset.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.FloatingPlacement
files.Summary: Where a floating picture, shape or text box sits and how text wraps around it (Word's anchor): position by alignment or offset from a reference area, wrap mode and side, the distances text keeps, and the stacking order. Immutable; set a new one to move the object.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.FontFeatures
files.Summary: OpenType features turned on or off for some text, such as liga=0 for no standard ligatures or tnum for tabular figures. A feature's value is 1 for on, 0 for off, or a number for features that choose among alternates. The set is compared by value, so two runs with the same features share formatting.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Footnote
files.Summary: A footnote or endnote: the reference mark in the text, which holds the note's own text as a story (Phase 6 design Q8). The mark is numbered automatically unless it has a .

files.Title: Egap.Documents.FormatBase
files.Summary: A set of formatting properties as Word keeps them (Phase 6 design Q5): every property is nullable, and null means "not set here", so the value comes from the style, the document defaults or the application. The format of a node or style reports each change to its document; a format made with new stands alone, for passing to the methods that copy it.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.FormatRevision
files.Summary: A tracked formatting change: who changed the formatting, when, and what it was before.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.GridAutoFlow
files.Summary: Which way a grid's automatic placement fills cells, and whether it goes back to fill holes.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.GridContainer
files.Summary: A grid container (CSS grid): items placed in cells of column and row tracks, by line, by named area or automatically, and spanning several. The page flow breaks between rows; DOCX writes the container as a borderless table.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.GridItem
files.Summary: An item of a : blocks in a box placed in one cell or spanning several. A line number counts from 1 at the grid's start, and from -1 at the end of the explicit grid; null leaves the item to automatic placement.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.GridLayout
files.Summary: How a grid container lays out its items (CSS grid): the column and row tracks, the size of tracks it adds, named areas, automatic placement, gaps and alignment. Immutable; set a new one to change it.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.GridTrack
files.Summary: A grid column or row: its least and greatest size (CSS minmax). A single size is both, except a fraction, which grows from its content's size as CSS's 1fr does.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.GridTrackSize
files.Summary: One limit of a grid track's size: a length, a share of the space, or a size from the content.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.GridTrackUnit
files.Summary: What a grid track size is given in.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.GroupPaging
files.Summary: How a group of blocks (a block content control) is placed across pages. Word keeps the blocks but not these settings, which only Egap's layout follows.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.HeaderFooter
files.Summary: A section's header or footer of one .

files.Title: Egap.Documents.HeaderFooterCollection
files.Summary: A section's headers and footers: at most one of each kind.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.HeaderFooterKind
files.Summary: Which pages a header or footer is for.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.HighlightColor
files.Summary: Text highlighting colours, the sixteen Word offers.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.HorizontalAnchor
files.Summary: What a floating object's horizontal position is measured from.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.HtmlFormat
files.Summary: HTML read into the model: parsed by AngleSharp as browsers parse it, styled through Egami.Css's cascade with HTML's default style sheet, and the computed styles mapped onto paragraphs, runs, lists, tables, and flex and grid containers; positioned boxes become floating text boxes.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.HtmlLoadOptions
files.Summary: How HTML is read (Phase 6 design Q14 to Q16).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.HtmlSaveOptions
files.Summary: How the model is written as HTML (Phase 6 design Q16).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Hyperlink
files.Summary: A hyperlink: the inlines it holds link to an address, a bookmark in the document, or both.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.IMergeData
files.Summary: One record of data for a mail merge: the value of each merge field, and the records of each repeated region. Implement it to stream records from any source; makes one from dictionaries, rows or objects.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ImageData
files.Summary: Image bytes as a file stores them, with their media type, such as image/png or image/x-emf.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Inline
files.Summary: A node that goes into a paragraph: a run of text, a tab or a break. Fields, hyperlinks, bookmarks, notes, comments and drawings join in Build Plan task 5.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.InlineContentControl
files.Summary: A content control around inlines inside a paragraph.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Island
files.Summary: An inline kept whole (Phase 6 design Q4): a format's raw markup for an equation, chart, SmartArt diagram, OLE object and the like, with the picture the file stores for it, so it survives a round trip and draws as that picture.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.IslandKind
files.Summary: What a kept island holds (Phase 6 design Q4): content the model keeps whole, as raw markup, drawn as its picture.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.AreaBox
files.Summary: A page area (body column, header, footer, notes or margin box) holding block boxes.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.CaretAffinity
files.Summary: Which side of a line break a position belongs to where one index is both the end of a line and the start of the next.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.CellBorders
files.Summary: A cell's four borders as the layout resolved them; null where there is none.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.CellBox
files.Summary: A table cell, with its blocks, borders and shading.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.ContainerBox
files.Summary: A flex or grid container, or a group of blocks with a box, or the part of one on this page or column: its box and the boxes inside it.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.DocumentLayout
files.Summary: A document laid out into pages (Phase 6 design Q11 and Q13): an immutable snapshot, each page a tree of boxes linked to the model nodes they show. An edit to the document needs a new layout.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.DocumentPosition
files.Summary: A place in the laid-out text (Phase 6 design Q13, Build Plan task 21b): a paragraph and an index into its text as the layout shows it (field results in place of their codes, without the list label), with the side of a line break. gives the model inline and offset it falls in.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.FontSettings
files.Summary: Where the layout engine finds fonts (Phase 6 design Q12): the document's embedded fonts first, then the caller's collections, then the system's, then metric-compatible substitutes from Egami.Fonts.Substitutes, then a last resort. Every font the document names and the chain could not give as asked is reported as a .

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.FontSubstitution
files.Summary: One font the layout could not use as the document asked, and what it used instead.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.FontSubstitutionReason
files.Summary: Why a font the document asked for was not used as asked.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.ItemBox
files.Summary: A flex or grid item, or the part of one on this page or column: its box and its blocks.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.LayoutBox
files.Summary: One box of a laid-out page (Phase 6 design Q13): its place on the page, the model node it shows, and the boxes inside it. Boxes are immutable; a new layout makes new boxes.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.LayoutDrawObserver
files.Summary: Told what is drawing, so the target canvas can group its output: PDF export marks each line and picture with its structure element and the rest as artifacts (Phase 6 Build Plan task 22). Every Begin is matched by its End, and calls nest as the boxes do.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.LayoutException
files.Summary: Thrown by a strict layout () when content cannot be laid out as written; names the node and the page, so the code or template that made it can be fixed.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.LayoutOptions
files.Summary: How lays a document out.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.LayoutProblem
files.Summary: Why a strict layout failed.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.LayoutRect
files.Summary: A rectangle on a page in points, from the page's top left corner.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.LineBox
files.Summary: One line of a paragraph: Egami's laid-out line placed on the page.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.ObjectBox
files.Summary: A picture, shape or island in a line or floating on the page.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.PageArea
files.Summary: What part of a page a box belongs to.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.PageLayout
files.Summary: One laid-out page: its size, its number as printed, and its areas.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.PageRect
files.Summary: A caret or selection rectangle on a page.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.ParagraphBox
files.Summary: A paragraph, or the part of one on this page or column, holding its lines.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.RowBox
files.Summary: A table row on this page or column.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.ScaledBox
files.Summary: A group of blocks drawn smaller so it fits where it is (): its children are laid out times wider than the box, from its top left corner, and drawn scaled down about that corner.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Layout.TableBox
files.Summary: A table, or the rows of one on this page or column.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.LayoutAlignment
files.Summary: How boxes line up along a container's axis: flex and grid containers and their items use the same values.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.LineSpacingRule
files.Summary: How is read.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.List
files.Summary: A list paragraphs belong to (Word's num): a and, per level, an optional new start or level of its own. Paragraphs join it through or their style; gives the computed label, such as "3.2.a".

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ListCollection
files.Summary: A document's lists and list definitions (Phase 6 design Q6): Word's numbering part. and make a list with Word's default bulleted or numbered levels.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ListDefinition
files.Summary: A list definition (Word's abstractNum): nine levels with their numbering, labels and indents. Lists () use a definition; lists that share one continue each other's numbering unless one restarts.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ListKind
files.Summary: How a list definition's levels are meant to be used, as Word records it.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ListLabel
files.Summary: A paragraph's computed list label.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ListLabelSuffix
files.Summary: What follows a list label before the paragraph's text.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ListLevel
files.Summary: One level of a list definition: where numbering starts, how numbers are written and the label's text, alignment and formatting, and the indents its paragraphs get (Phase 6 design Q6, Word's lvl).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ListLevelOverride
files.Summary: A change to one level of one list: a new start number, or a whole level of its own (Word's lvlOverride).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ListStyle
files.Summary: A list style (Word's numbering style): names the list its paragraphs and list definitions follow.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.MailMergeOptions
files.Summary: How a mail merge fills a template.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.MarginBox
files.Summary: Content in one of the page margins, drawn on every page of its section (or only on the first): text such as a title or "Page 3 of 9" with PAGE and NUMPAGES fields, as CSS's margin boxes hold. Headers and footers still apply; margin boxes sit beside them and do not move the body.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.MarginBoxCollection
files.Summary: A section's margin boxes: at most one for each position, and one more for each on the first page.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.MarginBoxPosition
files.Summary: Where a sits in the page margins: the sixteen boxes of CSS Paged Media, three along each edge and one in each corner.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.MarkdownExtensions
files.Summary: The Markdown extensions the reader understands beyond CommonMark (Phase 6 design Q17).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.MarkdownFormat
files.Summary: Reads Markdown into a and writes documents as GitHub Flavored Markdown: CommonMark 0.31 with GitHub's tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks and footnotes, and YAML front matter, parsed by Markdig. Headings take the Heading 1 to 6 styles, code the HTML Code and HTML Preformatted styles, lists Word list definitions built from their nesting. Writing says in warnings what Markdown cannot hold.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.MarkdownImage
files.Summary: An image the Markdown writer hands to .

files.Title: Egap.Documents.MarkdownImageMode
files.Summary: What the Markdown writer does with pictures that have no address of their own.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.MarkdownLoadOptions
files.Summary: How reads Markdown.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.MarkdownSaveOptions
files.Summary: How writes Markdown.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.MergeData
files.Summary: Merge data from dictionaries, rows of values with column names, and objects.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Node
files.Summary: One node of a document tree: the document itself, a section, a story, a block such as a paragraph or table, or an inline such as a run of text. Every node belongs to one for its whole life and sits in at most one place in that document's tree; a node made for one document goes into another through .

files.Title: Egap.Documents.NodeCollection<T>
files.Summary: The children of one kind a node holds, such as a story's blocks or a paragraph's inlines. The item type keeps wrong children out at compile time (a run cannot go into a story); adding also refuses a node of another document, a node already in the tree and a node that holds the parent.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.NoteKind
files.Summary: Whether a note is a footnote or an endnote.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.NoteStory
files.Summary: The text of a footnote or endnote.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.NumberStyle
files.Summary: How page numbers are written.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.PageOrientation
files.Summary: Page orientation.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.PageSetup
files.Summary: A section's page setup: paper size, orientation, margins, columns, page numbering and where it starts. Every property is nullable: null means not set here.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Paragraph
files.Summary: A paragraph: a list of inlines (runs of text, tabs, breaks and the rest) ended by a paragraph mark.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ParagraphAlignment
files.Summary: How a paragraph's lines line up between its indents.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ParagraphFormat
files.Summary: Paragraph formatting: alignment, indents, spacing, keep rules, tabs, borders and shading (Word's paragraph properties). Every property is nullable: null means not set here.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ParagraphStyle
files.Summary: A paragraph style: paragraph formatting and the character formatting of its text.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.HtmlStamp
files.Summary: Stamps made from HTML, laid out by Egap.Documents.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.ILayoutRegionDetector
files.Summary: Supplies regions and roles for a page from outside Egap's own rules, such as a layout model the caller already runs (design Q1): Egap ships no model, and this is the place one plugs in. A region the detector names takes precedence over what the rules would find there; the rules still group the text inside it into lines and paragraphs.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.IReadingOrderDetector
files.Summary: Orders a page's blocks, tables and figures, in place of Egap's XY cut.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.ITableDetector
files.Summary: Finds where a page's tables are, in place of Egap's own detection; Egap then finds the cells inside each area.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.LayoutBlock
files.Summary: A text block: a paragraph, heading, list item, caption, note, header or footer, with its lines.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.LayoutElement
files.Summary: A block, table or figure on a page: where it is, where it comes in reading order and how sure the analysis is.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.LayoutFigure
files.Summary: A figure: images and drawings with any text inside them.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.LayoutImage
files.Summary: An image where the page draws it.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.LayoutLine
files.Summary: A line of text with its words.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.LayoutRegionHint
files.Summary: A region an found: what it is, where it is and how sure the detector is.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.LayoutRole
files.Summary: What a region of a page is (design Q4), the roles layout analysis finds and a region detector can name.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.LayoutTable
files.Summary: A table: its cells on a grid of by . A table from a tagged PDF keeps the tags' cells and their order, with spans taken from the page's rules or text where the tags give none (as Word's do not).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.LayoutTableCell
files.Summary: A table cell.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.LayoutThresholds
files.Summary: Every threshold the geometric stages use (design Q1: every threshold an option). Distances are in multiples of the text size unless they say otherwise, so they hold for any font size. The defaults are tuned against the comparison data sets and may change in a minor version; the properties themselves stay.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.LayoutWord
files.Summary: A word with the font it is mostly set in.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.OutlineFrom
files.Summary: What a PDF's outline (its bookmarks pane) is built from.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PageBand
files.Summary: A header or footer that puts on every page ( and ), in the top or bottom margin: plain text in up to three places (), or HTML styled with the page's own CSS (). Both take the : {page}, {total-pages}, {label}, {date}, {time}, {title} and {file}.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PageMargins
files.Summary: The space between the page edges and the content, on each side.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PdfAutoTagFigure
files.Summary: A figure tagged without alternate text.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PdfAutoTagReport
files.Summary: What did.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PdfAutoTagger
files.Summary: Tags an untagged PDF from its layout (design Q11, Build Plan task 14): a structure tree through Phase 5's model, with headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, figures, captions, quotes, code and notes in reading order, page headers and footers and decoration marked as artifacts, and the page content wrapped in marked content that points at its element. Figures get no alternate text: the report lists them, and writing it stays with the caller.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PdfConvert
files.Summary: One-line conversions to PDF: HTML, Markdown, DOCX and images in, a PDF file or an open out. Each reads the input with Egap.Documents, lays it out and exports it as does.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PdfConvertOptions
files.Summary: How turns HTML, Markdown, DOCX and images into PDF.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PdfExport
files.Summary: Flow documents saved as PDF (Phase 6 design Q2, Build Plan task 22): each laid-out page drawn on a , with link annotations for hyperlinks, an outline, named destinations for bookmarks, the document's properties as metadata, and on request tags and PDF/A.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PdfExportOptions
files.Summary: How a flow document is saved as PDF (Phase 6 design Q2, Build Plan task 22).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PdfLayoutAnalyzer
files.Summary: Layout analysis of PDF pages (design Q10, Build Plan task 10): blocks with roles, tables and figures in reading order, without building a document model. Tagged pages whose tags pass a sanity check are read from their tags (design Q2); others by geometric rules (design Q1, Q3 to Q7), every threshold an option and the main stages replaceable through .

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PdfLayoutOptions
files.Summary: How layout analysis runs (design Q2, Q5, Q10): whether tags are trusted, which tables are looked for, the stages a caller replaces, and every threshold.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PdfPageLayout
files.Summary: What layout analysis found on one page (design Q10): text blocks with their roles, tables and figures, each with its bounds and place in the page's reading order. Bounds are in points on the displayed page: y down from the top left of the crop box, the page's rotation applied, as draws by default.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PdfToDocument
files.Summary: PDF to the flow document model (design Q6 to Q8, Q10): layout analysis, then the pages joined into sections with styles, lists, tables, pictures, headers and footers and footnotes, ready to save as Word, HTML or Markdown through Egap.Documents.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PdfToDocumentMode
files.Summary: How turns pages into a document (design Q8).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PdfToDocumentOptions
files.Summary: How analyses a PDF and builds the document.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PdfToDocumentWarning
files.Summary: What could not carry over as it was, on which page.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.PdfToDocumentWarningKind
files.Summary: The kinds of .

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.TableCsv
files.Summary: Detected tables as CSV (RFC 4180; Build Plan task 19): one CSV per table, a table that runs on across pages written once with its repeated header left out, merged cells repeated across their span or left empty, and the number of header rows given with each so a reader can treat them as headers.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.TableCsvFile
files.Summary: A table written as CSV.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.TableCsvOptions
files.Summary: How writes tables.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.TableDetection
files.Summary: Which tables layout analysis looks for (design Q5).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Pdf.TableOfContentsMode
files.Summary: Whether gives the PDF a table of contents built from the headings.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Picture
files.Summary: A picture in the text: an image of given size, in the line or floating.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.PreviewOptions
files.Summary: Where sends a document's pages, and how sharp they are drawn.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Reports.ColumnBuilder
files.Summary: Elements one under another.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Reports.Container
files.Summary: A place in a report that takes one element (text, an image, a column, a row, a table, a grid, a barcode, a form field or a component), with the box, alignment, style and paging settings set on it first: each setting returns the container, and the element ends the chain.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Reports.Fields
files.Summary: The placeholders text in a report can hold for page fields: {page} and {total-pages}.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Reports.GridBuilder
files.Summary: Elements in a grid of tracks.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Reports.IComponent
files.Summary: A reusable part of a report: it composes itself into the container it is given.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Reports.PageDescriptor
files.Summary: One page of a report, repeated as the content needs: size, margins, header, footer and content.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Reports.Report
files.Summary: Builds a document from code with nested lambdas: pages with a header, a footer and content, and in them columns, rows, tables, grids, text, images and barcodes, each with its box and paging settings. The result is an ordinary , so the same report saves as PDF, DOCX or HTML and lays out with the same page flow.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Reports.ReportBuilder
files.Summary: What gives the composing code: the document's properties, styles and pages.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Reports.RowBuilder
files.Summary: Elements side by side: each of a fixed width, its content's width, or a share of what is left.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Reports.TableBuilder
files.Summary: A table: columns, cells filled in order row by row, and header and footer rows that repeat on every page.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Reports.TableColumns
files.Summary: The columns of a table: fixed widths and shares of what is left.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Reports.TextBuilder
files.Summary: The spans of one paragraph, each with its own style.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Reports.TextDescriptor
files.Summary: A paragraph of text a container made: its look set by a style chain.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Reports.TextStyle
files.Summary: How text in a report looks: font, size, weight, slant, lines, colours, letter spacing and line height. Immutable: each method returns a changed copy, so a style can be kept and shared (TextStyle.Default.FontSize(18).Bold()). What a style leaves unset comes from the style of the text around it.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ResolvedParagraphFormat
files.Summary: A paragraph's effective formatting (): every property with its final value, styles and defaults applied, tab stops added up. Where neither the document nor Word gives a value, Word's defaults apply.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ResolvedRunFormat
files.Summary: A run's effective formatting (): every property with its final value, styles and defaults applied, theme fonts named. Where neither the document nor Word gives a value, Word's own defaults apply (10 pt, Times New Roman, automatic colour).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Revision
files.Summary: A tracked insertion, deletion or move on a node: what, who and when.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.RevisionKind
files.Summary: What a tracked change did (Phase 6 design Q8: changes are marks on the nodes they change).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Row
files.Summary: A table row: its cells in order.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.RowFormat
files.Summary: Table row formatting: height, header repeat and page splitting. Every property is nullable: null means not set here.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.RowHeightRule
files.Summary: How a row's height is read.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Run
files.Summary: A run of text with one formatting (Build Plan task 3).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.RunFormat
files.Summary: Character formatting: font, size, colour, bold and the rest (Word's run properties). Every property is nullable: null means not set here.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Section
files.Summary: A part of a document with its own page setup (Build Plan task 3), a body and up to three headers and three footers (first page, odd or every page, even pages).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.SectionStart
files.Summary: Where a section starts.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Shading
files.Summary: Shading behind text, a paragraph or a cell: a fill colour, a pattern and the pattern's colour.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ShadingPattern
files.Summary: A shading pattern: Word's set, from clear (fill only) to solid (pattern colour only) by percentages and hatches.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Shape
files.Summary: A shape in the text, in the line or floating, with a fill and an outline, and optionally text inside it (a text box, Phase 6 design Q11).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ShapeKind
files.Summary: The shape a draws (Word's preset geometry), from the common ones.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Story
files.Summary: Content that flows on its own: a section's body or a header or footer. Footnotes, comments and text boxes join in Build Plan task 5.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Style
files.Summary: A named set of formatting that paragraphs, runs or tables point at, as in Word (Phase 6 design Q5). A style can be based on another of the same type, taking every property it does not set from it. Styles belong to one document's .

files.Title: Egap.Documents.StyleCollection
files.Summary: A document's styles, by id, with the document defaults every style builds on (Word's docDefaults). A new document has Word's Normal paragraph style, Default Paragraph Font and Normal Table, with Word 2013+'s defaults (11 pt body font from the theme, 8 pt after paragraphs, 1.08 line spacing); adds the others Word knows, such as headings.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.StyleType
files.Summary: The kind of a .

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Tab
files.Summary: A tab: the text moves on to the paragraph's next tab stop.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TabAlignment
files.Summary: How text lines up at a tab stop.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TabLeader
files.Summary: What fills the space before a tab stop.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TabStop
files.Summary: A tab stop: where, how text lines up, and the leader.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Table
files.Summary: A table: rows of cells, each cell holding blocks, so tables nest. Rows need not have the same number of cells; merged cells and widths come with the table format in Build Plan task 3.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TableAlignment
files.Summary: Where a table sits between the margins.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TableFormat
files.Summary: Table formatting: width, alignment, layout, default cell margins, borders, shading and style options. Every property is nullable: null means not set here.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TableLayoutKind
files.Summary: How a table's column widths are found.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TableStyle
files.Summary: A table style: formatting for the whole table and, apart, for its first and last rows and columns, bands and corners.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TableStyleConditional
files.Summary: The formatting a table style gives one .

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TableStyleRegion
files.Summary: The parts of a table a table style can format apart (Word's conditional formatting).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TableWidth
files.Summary: A table or cell width: automatic, in points or in per cent.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TextBoxStory
files.Summary: The text inside a text box.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TextColumn
files.Summary: One text column of a section with unequal columns: its width and the space after it, in points.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TextDirection
files.Summary: Which way text runs in a cell or section.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TextFormat
files.Summary: Plain text read line by line into paragraphs, and the document written as plain text in reading order, for search and indexing (Phase 6 Build Plan task 8c): one line per paragraph, list labels before their text with a tab, table rows as tab-separated cells, text boxes after the paragraph they are anchored in, equations as their text. Field codes, deleted and hidden text, comments and pictures are left out.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TextMatch
files.Summary: A match found: where it is in its paragraph's text as Find sees it (runs joined, a tab as \t, a line break as \v, deleted text left out unless the options keep it) and the text it matched.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TextSaveOptions
files.Summary: How writes plain text.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.Theme
files.Summary: A document theme: twelve colours and the major (headings) and minor (body) fonts, which runs and styles name instead of fixed values, so changing the theme restyles the document. A new document has Word's Office theme (2013 to 2022).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ThemeColor
files.Summary: Which of a theme's twelve colours a names, as Word's themes have them.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ThemeColors
files.Summary: A theme's twelve colours.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.ThemeFont
files.Summary: Which theme font a run's font slot names.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TrackedChange
files.Summary: One tracked change in a document (Phase 6 design Q8): a or on a node, which can be accepted or rejected on its own.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TrackedChangeCollection
files.Summary: A document's tracked changes in document order, to read, accept or reject.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.TrackedChangeTarget
files.Summary: What part of a node a is about.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.UnderlineStyle
files.Summary: How text is underlined, as Word's underline types.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.VerticalAlignment
files.Summary: Where content sits vertically in a cell, or a page's text in a section.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.VerticalAnchor
files.Summary: What a floating object's vertical position is measured from.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.VerticalMerge
files.Summary: A cell's part in a vertical merge.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.VerticalTextPosition
files.Summary: Raised or lowered text.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.VisitorAction
files.Summary: What a wants the walk to do next.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.WidthUnit
files.Summary: How a table, cell or row width or height is given.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.WordBreak
files.Summary: Where lines may break inside words.

files.Title: Egap.Documents.WrapMode
files.Summary: How text flows around a floating object (Phase 6 design Q11: all six of Word's wrap modes).

files.Title: Egap.Documents.WrapSide
files.Summary: Which sides of a floating object text flows on.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.BlankPageOptions
files.Summary: When takes a page for blank (Phase 7 design Q15).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.BookletBinding
files.Summary: Which edge a booklet is bound on.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.BookletOptions
files.Summary: How lays a saddle-stitched booklet out.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.DeskewOptions
files.Summary: How straightens scans.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.GridOptions
files.Summary: How puts every page on one sheet.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.Length
files.Summary: A length on the page, held in points (1/72 inch) and made from points, millimetres, centimetres or inches, so sizes in different units cannot be mixed up. It converts to and from a in points without a cast, so it can be passed wherever a size in points is asked for, and a plain number still works wherever a is.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.NUpOptions
files.Summary: How lays pages out (Phase 7 design Q9).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.NUpOrder
files.Summary: The order pages fill the cells of an N-up sheet.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PadesLevel
files.Summary: The PAdES baseline level a signature is made at (ETSI EN 319 142-1; Phase 5 design Q4).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfAConformance
files.Summary: A PDF/A part and conformance level a file claims (ISO 19005; Phase 5 design Q11).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfAConvertOptions
files.Summary: Options for .

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfAConverter
files.Summary: Converts documents to PDF/A and checks them against the rules Egap enforces (Phase 5 design Q12, Q13). Conversion keeps the file's objects and fixes what it can, reporting every fix; if any rule cannot be met, nothing is changed. A converted document saves by the part's rules from then on: written whole, without encryption, as the part's version.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfAIssue
files.Summary: One PDF/A rule a document broke (Phase 5 design Q12, Q13), and whether conversion can put it right or did.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfAReport
files.Summary: What a PDF/A conversion did or a check found (Phase 5 design Q12, Q13). A conversion that could not meet every rule changed nothing; its report lists every issue, the ones it would have fixed with set.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfAction
files.Summary: An action (12.6): a thin view over its dictionary, typed by /S through . JavaScript and any action type Egap does not know are plain s: kept and written back as they are, never run. Two views are equal when they wrap the same dictionary.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfAnnotation
files.Summary: An annotation (12.5): a thin view over its dictionary, typed by /Subtype through (Phase 2 Q10). Subtypes Egap has no class for (Sound, Movie, Screen, 3D, RichMedia, PrinterMark, TrapNet, Watermark, Projection and any unknown one) are plain s, read and written through . Two views are equal when they wrap the same dictionary.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfAnnotationCollection
files.Summary: A page's annotations (12.5): its /Annots array, in order, each annotation once. Entries that are not dictionaries are left out, as pdf.js and PDFium leave them out. Adding and removing edit the array in place, keep each annotation's /P pointing at the page, and keep popups with the annotations they belong to.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfAnnotationFlags
files.Summary: Annotation flags (12.5.3, table 167).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfAnnotationRendering
files.Summary: Which annotations a render draws (design Q12).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfAntialiasing
files.Summary: What a render anti-aliases (design Q11).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfAppearanceKind
files.Summary: Which appearance of an annotation (12.5.5).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfArray
files.Summary: A PDF array.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfAttachment
files.Summary: An embedded file (7.11.4): a thin view over its file specification dictionary, which holds the embedded file stream in /EF. Two views are equal when they wrap the same file specification.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfAttachmentCollection
files.Summary: The document's embedded files (7.11.4): the catalog's /Names /EmbeddedFiles name tree, in key order. Adding and removing edit the tree in place (Phase 2 Q3) and keep the catalog's /AF associated files (PDF 2.0) in step.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfAttachmentRelationship
files.Summary: How an attached file relates to the document (/AFRelationship, ISO 32000-2 14.13.2).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfBatesSequence
files.Summary: A Bates numbering sequence (Phase 7 design Q11): numbers with a prefix, a suffix and a fixed number of digits, continuing across every document stamped with it, so a set of documents is numbered page by page from one start.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfBoolean
files.Summary: A PDF boolean. There are two instances, and .

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfBorderStyle
files.Summary: A border style (12.5.4, table 168).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfButtonOptions
files.Summary: How a new check box or radio group works.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfByteRange
files.Summary: One range of signed bytes: Length bytes from Start.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfByteRangeIssues
files.Summary: What is wrong with a signature's /ByteRange (Phase 5 design, 5.1); when nothing is.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfCanvas
files.Summary: An Egami canvas that draws onto a PDF page: the same drawing code that fills a raster writes PDF operators here (Phase 3, hub Q10). Paths, strokes, clips, opacity and blend modes become vector content; what PDF cannot express is drawn into an image at and placed instead, with a warning.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfCanvasCoordinates
files.Summary: Which coordinates a draws in (Phase 3 design Q13).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfCanvasOptions
files.Summary: How a draws onto a page.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfCanvasPlacement
files.Summary: Where new drawing goes on a page that already has content (Phase 3 design Q5).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfCaretAnnotation
files.Summary: A caret annotation (12.5.6.11, PDF 1.5): marks where text is to be inserted.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfCertificateSeed
files.Summary: Certificate constraints of a seed value (/Cert, ISO 32000-2, Table 238).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfCertificateSeedFlags
files.Summary: Which certificate seed values a signer must follow (/Ff of a certificate seed value dictionary, ISO 32000-2, Table 238).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfCertification
files.Summary: The changes a certification signature allows after it (DocMDP /P, ISO 32000-2, 12.8.2.2); the values are the numbers in the file.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfChangeVerdict
files.Summary: How a change made after a signature is judged (Phase 5 design Q8).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfCheckBoxField
files.Summary: A check box (12.7.5.2.3): on or off.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfChoiceField
files.Summary: A choice field (12.7.5.4): a combo box or list box of options.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfChoiceFieldOptions
files.Summary: How a new combo box or list box works.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfChoiceOption
files.Summary: An option of a choice field: the value exported when it is selected, and the text shown.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfCircleAnnotation
files.Summary: A circle annotation (12.5.6.8): an ellipse drawn inside the annotation's rectangle.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfClipPath
files.Summary: A clip the content set (8.5.4): a path, the transformation it was set under, and its fill rule.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfColor
files.Summary: A colour as content sets it (8.6): its colour space, as named in the content and resolved through the resources (a name such as DeviceRGB, or an array such as [/ICCBased 7 0 R]), its components, and for a pattern the pattern's resource name.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfComboBoxField
files.Summary: A combo box (12.7.5.4): a drop-down list, editable or not.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfCompare
files.Summary: Compares two PDF documents (Phase 7 design 7.4): a text pass that diffs the words of both documents in reading order and matches pages by the words they share, and a visual pass that renders each matching pair of pages and boxes the pixels that differ. Both documents must stay open while the comparison is used, as markup reads the new one.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfCompareOptions
files.Summary: How compares two documents (Phase 7 design Q12 and Q13).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfComparedWord
files.Summary: A word compare read, with the page (1-based) and box (default user space) it is on.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfComparison
files.Summary: What changed between two documents (Phase 7 design Q12 and Q13): text changes found by a word-level diff over the whole documents, so text that only moved to another page is no change; how pages match; and where matching pages render differently. writes a copy of the new document with the changes marked.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfCompression
files.Summary: Whether a rewrite packs objects into object streams and the cross-reference into a stream (design Q7).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfContent
files.Summary: The operations of a content stream (8.2): a page's content, a form XObject's, a Type 3 glyph's, or content built from scratch. It is a plain list (Phase 3 design Q3): operations can be read, inserted, removed and replaced, and operators the spec does not define are kept, so content round-trips whatever it holds.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfContentWalker
files.Summary: Walks content with its resources and tracks the graphics state (8.4) through it: the transformation matrix, q and Q, the text state and matrices, colours and colour spaces, clips, graphics state dictionaries and marked content. It descends into form XObjects and Type 3 glyph procedures. Derive from it and override the On methods to see paths, glyphs, images, shadings and marked content with the state they are drawn in (Phase 3 design Q3).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfContentWriter
files.Summary: Writes a content stream (8.2) operator by operator, every operator of ISO 32000-2 table A.1 included, into bytes for a page, form XObject or appearance stream. Operands are written as the object writer writes objects, so names and strings are escaped, and numbers have no exponents: whole numbers as integers, others rounded to five decimals, or to six significant digits below 1. Saves, text objects and marked content are counted, and refuses content that leaves one open, which a viewer would misread.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfCreateOptions
files.Summary: Options for .

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfDestination
files.Summary: An explicit destination (12.3.2.2): a page and how to show it. The page is a reference to a page of this document, or a page index (from 0) for a destination in another file (). A coordinate or zoom of null leaves the viewer's current value unchanged.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfDestinationFit
files.Summary: How a destination fits its page in the window (12.3.2.2).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfDictionary
files.Summary: A PDF dictionary: names mapped to objects, kept in the order they were added so a rewrite keeps the file's order.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfDocument
files.Summary: Pages made from images, and pages written as image files.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfEncryption
files.Summary: How a save encrypts the document: keep the encryption it was opened with, drop it, or apply new AES-256 encryption.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfEncryptionKind
files.Summary: The kinds of .

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfException
files.Summary: The exception thrown when a PDF file cannot be read, or, in strict mode, when it needs any repair.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfField
files.Summary: A form field (12.7.4): a thin view over its field dictionary. Terminal fields are typed by /FT and their flags: , , , , , and ; non-terminal fields, and terminal fields of an unknown type, are plain s. Two views are equal when they wrap the same dictionary.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfFieldFlags
files.Summary: Field flags (12.7.4.1, tables 227, 229, 231 and 233). Some bits mean different things for different field types.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfFieldLock
files.Summary: A field lock (ISO 32000-2, 12.7.5.5 and 12.8.2.4): the fields a signature makes read-only, from a signature field's /Lock before signing or from a signature's FieldMDP reference after.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfFieldLockAction
files.Summary: Which fields a field lock covers (/Action, ISO 32000-2, Table 236).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfFieldOptions
files.Summary: What every new form field can have: a tooltip, flags, and how its widget looks.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfFileAttachmentAnnotation
files.Summary: A file attachment annotation (12.5.6.15): a file embedded at a point on the page, shown as an icon.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfFindOptions
files.Summary: How and the methods like it search.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfFlattenFilter
files.Summary: Which annotations flattening draws, as qpdf's --flatten-annotations chooses them; hidden ones never.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfFont
files.Summary: A font a page's text uses (Phase 3 design Q7): read-only. It says what kind of font it is, its names, flags and metrics, how its strings split into codes, each code's width and glyph name, and the text a code stands for, through the font's ToUnicode map first, then its encoding's glyph names through the Adobe Glyph List. Fonts are read leniently: what a file gets wrong gives no answer rather than an exception.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfFontCollection
files.Summary: The fonts a page's resources name (/Font), by resource name: page.Fonts["F1"] is the font /F1 12 Tf selects. Read when asked, so it always shows the resources as they are.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfFontFlags
files.Summary: The flags of a font descriptor (9.8.2, table 121).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfFontType
files.Summary: The kind of a PDF font, its /Subtype (9.5).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfForm
files.Summary: The interactive form (12.7): a thin view over the catalog's /AcroForm dictionary, whose /Fields are the roots of the field tree. A document without one has no fields. Fields are read leniently: loops, entries that are not dictionaries and trees deeper than 64 levels are skipped, as pdf.js and qpdf skip them.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfFormXObject
files.Summary: A page drawn as a form XObject (Phase 7 design Q8): a whole page that another page can draw, scaled and placed, as imposition and page stamps do. Its space is the page as a viewer shows it: points from the bottom left of the crop box, rotation applied, by .

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfFreeTextAnnotation
files.Summary: A free text annotation (12.5.6.6): text drawn straight on the page, in a box or with a callout line.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfGlyph
files.Summary: One glyph shown by a text operator, as a reports it: the code shown, the font and the text rendering matrix (9.4.4) that maps the glyph from text space, scaled by the font size, to the space the walk started in.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfGoToAction
files.Summary: A go-to action (12.6.4.2): goes to a destination in this document, given explicitly or by name.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfGoToEmbeddedAction
files.Summary: An embedded go-to action (12.6.4.4): goes to a destination in an embedded or embedding PDF file.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfGoToRemoteAction
files.Summary: A remote go-to action (12.6.4.3): goes to a destination in another PDF file, whose pages are given by index.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfGraphicsState
files.Summary: The graphics state (8.4) as a tracks it: what q saves and Q restores. The text matrices are not in it; they belong to the text object (9.4.2) and are on the walker.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfHideAction
files.Summary: A hide action (12.6.4.10): hides or shows annotations or fields.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfHighlightAnnotation
files.Summary: A highlight annotation (12.5.6.10): text marked as with a highlighter.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfHighlightMode
files.Summary: How a link or widget looks while pressed (12.5.6.5, table 176).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfImage
files.Summary: An image a page draws (8.9): an image XObject or an inline image (Phase 3 design Q11). It gives the image's stored bytes and filters, so a JPEG can be saved as it is, and decodes to an Egami raster with its colour space, decode array and masks applied.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfImageEncoding
files.Summary: How stores a new image.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfImageOptions
files.Summary: How decodes an image (Phase 3 design Q11 and Q12).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfImagePageOptions
files.Summary: How images become pages in .

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfImportOptions
files.Summary: Options for importing pages.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfImpose
files.Summary: Imposition (Phase 7 design 7.2, Q9): new documents whose sheets draw the source's pages as form XObjects, placed and scaled. The source is never changed; it must stay open until the result is saved, which reads the pages' streams then. Every layout keeps each page's content, resources and printable annotations, shared once per source.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfInkAnnotation
files.Summary: An ink annotation (12.5.6.13): freehand strokes.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfInlineImage
files.Summary: An inline image (8.9.7): BI, its parameters, ID, its data and EI, kept as one operation with the data as stored. Its is BI and it has no operands.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfInteger
files.Summary: A PDF integer, held as 64 bits.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfInvoice
files.Summary: A Factur-X or ZUGFeRD e-invoice in a PDF: the invoice's XML (UN/CEFACT Cross Industry Invoice) attached to a PDF/A-3 document, with the Factur-X schema in the document's XMP saying the file name, the profile and the version. The XML is the invoicing system's to write; Egap embeds it and reads it back.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfInvoiceOptions
files.Summary: How embeds an invoice.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfInvoiceProfile
files.Summary: The Factur-X and ZUGFeRD profile, how much of the invoice the XML holds.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfInvoiceStandard
files.Summary: The e-invoice standard an embedded invoice follows.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfLaunchAction
files.Summary: A launch action (12.6.4.6): opens a file or starts an application. Kept as it is; Egap never launches anything.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfLayer
files.Summary: An optional content group (8.11.2), a layer: a thin view over its dictionary. Its visibility and lock are read from and written to the document's default configuration (/OCProperties /D). Two views are equal when they wrap the same dictionary.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfLayerCollection
files.Summary: The document's optional content groups (8.11), its layers, from the catalog's /OCProperties /OCGs, each once in the order listed. Removing a layer takes it out of the configurations; the content it marks stays on the pages unless is asked to remove it too.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfLimitException
files.Summary: The exception thrown when a file goes past one of the limits in . It is never a warning, even outside strict mode: going on could exhaust memory or time.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfLineAnnotation
files.Summary: A line annotation (12.5.6.7): a straight line with optional endings and caption.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfLineEnding
files.Summary: A line ending style (12.5.6.7, table 179), named as in the file.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfLinkAnnotation
files.Summary: A link annotation (12.5.6.5): an area of the page that goes to a destination or runs an action.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfListBoxField
files.Summary: A list box (12.7.5.4): a scrolling list, with one or several selected.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfMarkedContent
files.Summary: A marked-content sequence or point (14.6): its tag and properties. Properties named in the resources (/OC /MC0 BDC) are looked up there; keeps the name.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfMarkedContentReference
files.Summary: A marked-content sequence a structure element owns: content tagged with an MCID on a page or in a form XObject.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfMarkupAnnotation
files.Summary: A markup annotation (12.5.6.2): one a reader writes on the page, with an author, a popup for its text, and replies.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfMatrix
files.Summary: A transformation matrix as PDF writes it (8.3.3): [a b c d e f], mapping a point (x, y) to (a·x + c·y + e, b·x + d·y + f).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfMetadata
files.Summary: The document's metadata (14.3) through one API over both stores (Phase 2 Q8): the document information dictionary (/Info in the trailer) and the XMP packet (the catalog's /Metadata stream). Reading prefers XMP when the packet has the property, as pdf.js does. Setting writes the Info entry and, when the document has an XMP packet or is PDF 2.0, the matching XMP property; a document before 2.0 without a packet gets none unless is called. Setting null removes the property from both.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfName
files.Summary: A PDF name, such as /Type. A name is a sequence of bytes, by convention UTF-8 text; is that text without the slash.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfNamedAction
files.Summary: A named action (12.6.4.11), such as NextPage, PrevPage, FirstPage or LastPage.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfNamedDestinations
files.Summary: A document's named destinations (12.3.2.4), found through both lookups: the /Dests name tree in the catalog's /Names (PDF 1.2 and later) and the older /Dests dictionary in the catalog (PDF 1.1). A name in both is taken from the name tree. New names go in the name tree, which is edited in place (Phase 2 Q3).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfNull
files.Summary: The PDF null object. There is one instance, .

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfObject
files.Summary: A PDF object (ISO 32000-2, 7.3): , , , , , , , , or a to an indirect object.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfObjectReference
files.Summary: An object a structure element owns (an OBJR): an annotation, such as a link or form widget, or an XObject.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfObjectTable
files.Summary: A document's indirect objects, by number. Objects load from the file the first time they are asked for; changing one, anywhere in its tree, marks it as changed, so an incremental save writes only what changed.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfOcrLayer
files.Summary: An invisible text layer over a scanned page (Phase 5 design Q16): the words OCR found, drawn in render mode 3 (neither filled nor stroked) in a glyphless font Egap builds, each word scaled to its box, so the page can be searched, selected and read aloud while it looks exactly as the scan. Words come from hOCR (Tesseract, Kraken, OCRmyPDF) or ALTO (ABBYY, libraries' digitisation) files, or from any OCR engine as word boxes. The page image is not touched.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfOcrLine
files.Summary: A recognised line of words, in reading order.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfOcrWord
files.Summary: A recognised word: its text and its box on the page, in PDF user space (Phase 5 design Q16).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfOperation
files.Summary: One operation of a content stream (8.2): an operator and its operands, such as 1 0 0 1 72 720 cm. Operations are values: they are never changed after they are made, so an edited content stream replaces operations instead of changing them, and the operand objects (arrays and dictionaries included) should be treated as read-only.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfOptimizeOptions
files.Summary: What does (Phase 7 design Q2 to Q7). A preset fills in the switches; each can be changed with with. , the default, never changes a pixel: it merges duplicates, subsets fonts, removes what nobody sees, codes bilevel images as CCITT G4, optimizes JPEG Huffman tables and writes object streams. , and also downsample images above 1.5 times their resolution and write photos as JPEG at their quality.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfOptimizeReport
files.Summary: What did (Phase 7 design 7.1): bytes before and after, by pass, and every image changed.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfOptimizeSavings
files.Summary: What each optimizer pass saved, in stored bytes before the file is written.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfOptimizedImage
files.Summary: One image the optimizer changed.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfOutline
files.Summary: The document outline (bookmarks, 12.3.3), from the catalog's /Outlines. A broken outline (chains that loop, wrong /Prev, /Parent or /Last, kids that are not dictionaries) is repaired in memory on first use with warnings, as pdf.js and qpdf read it. The outline dictionary is created by the first item added.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfOutlineItem
files.Summary: An outline item (12.3.3): a thin view over its dictionary, equal to another view of the same dictionary. It goes to a destination (/Dest) or runs an action (/A), and has a title, colour, style and open state.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfOutlineNode
files.Summary: A node of the document outline (12.3.3): the outline itself or one of its items. Children are read through /First and /Next; adding, removing and moving keep /First, /Last, /Prev, /Next, /Parent and the /Count of every node above in step, touching only the nodes involved.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPage
files.Summary: A page (7.7.3.3): a thin view over the page's dictionary, which it reads and writes directly, so anything it does not cover is still there in . Two views are equal when they wrap the same dictionary (Phase 2 Q1).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPageBox
files.Summary: Which of a page's boxes (14.11.2) a render shows.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPageCollection
files.Summary: A document's pages in order, numbered from 0 (Phase 2 Q2). The list is built on first use by walking the page tree from the catalog; only the tree's nodes are loaded, not the pages' content. A broken tree is repaired in memory with warnings, as pdf.js and PDFium read it.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPageLabelRange
files.Summary: A range of page labels (12.4.2): from the page at (from 0) up to the next range, labels are the prefix followed by a number in the given style, counting from .

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPageLabelStyle
files.Summary: How the number in a page label is written (12.4.2).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPageMatch
files.Summary: Which old page a new page matches; a page only one side has is added or removed.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPageRange
files.Summary: A choice of pages written as text, such as "1,3,5-10,z", that is turned into page numbers once the page count is known. Pass it to , and the page renderers, or turn it into page indices with for .

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPageSize
files.Summary: A sheet size in points, such as .

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPasswordException
files.Summary: The exception thrown when an encrypted file needs a password that was not given, or the password given is neither the user nor the owner password. Set and open the file again.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPath
files.Summary: A path as content builds it (8.5.2), in the user space it was built in: subpaths of lines and cubic curves. re becomes a closed subpath of four lines, and v and y become curves with both control points given.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPathPaint
files.Summary: How a path is painted (8.5.3): any mix of stroking, filling and clipping, or none for n on its own.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPathSegment
files.Summary: One segment of a path. For a curve, and are its control points.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPathVerb
files.Summary: What a path segment does (8.5.2).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPermissions
files.Summary: What the owner of an encrypted file allows (ISO 32000-2, Table 22). The flags are advisory: anyone who can open the file can read everything in it, so honouring them is the caller's job (design Q5). The values are the bits of /P.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPlacedImage
files.Summary: An image where a page draws it: the image and the matrix that maps its unit square into the page's default space.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPlaceholderValues
files.Summary: The values one page's placeholders are filled with, for .

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPlaceholders
files.Summary: The placeholders page furniture is written with, the same everywhere Egap fills text per page (stamps, and headers and footers on export): {page}, {total-pages} (also {pages}), {label} (the page label), {date}, {time}, {title} and {file}.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPoint
files.Summary: A point in default user space, as annotations give vertices, lines and quadrilaterals.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPolyLineAnnotation
files.Summary: A polyline annotation (12.5.6.9): an open line through its vertices, with optional endings.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPolygonAnnotation
files.Summary: A polygon annotation (12.5.6.9): a closed shape through its vertices.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPopupAnnotation
files.Summary: A popup annotation (12.5.6.14): the window that shows a markup annotation's text.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPreparedSignature
files.Summary: A signature waiting for its CMS (Phase 5 design Q3): the file is written with the space reserved, and is what a signing service signs. writes the CMS it returns into that space, in the same stream; a file prepared earlier, in another process, is completed with .

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfPushButtonField
files.Summary: A push button (12.7.5.2.2): runs an action and has no value.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfQuad
files.Summary: A quadrilateral on the page, such as the area of a matched run of text on one line, in default user space.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfRadioButtonField
files.Summary: A radio button group (12.7.5.2.4): one widget per button, at most one on.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfReadOptions
files.Summary: Options for opening a PDF file: the password, strict mode and the limits that protect against hostile files.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfReal
files.Summary: A PDF real number, held as a .

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfRectangle
files.Summary: A rectangle in PDF user space (7.9.5), as page boxes are given: the lower-left and upper-right corners, with y going up.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfRedactAnnotation
files.Summary: A redaction annotation (12.5.6.23, PDF 1.7): marks content to be removed. Applying redactions changes page content, which is layer 3; Phase 2 reads and writes the annotation only.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfRedactImages
files.Summary: What redaction does to an image the area covers (Phase 5 design Q9).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfRedactPaths
files.Summary: What redaction does to vector line art the area covers (Phase 5 design Q9).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfRedactionOptions
files.Summary: How redaction annotations are applied (Phase 5 design Q9).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfRedactionResult
files.Summary: What applying redactions removed (Phase 5 design Q9).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfReference
files.Summary: A reference to an indirect object: its object number and generation (12 0 R). References come from the document, from or , so they always resolve through it.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfRenderIntent
files.Summary: What a render is for, which decides the annotations (by their flags) and layers (by their usage) that show.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfRenderOptions
files.Summary: How a page is rendered (Phase 4 design Q3 and Q4): the resolution or a size to fit, which box shows, extra rotation, a region of the output for tiles, the intent, the background, annotations and anti-aliasing. The defaults draw the crop box at 72 dpi (one pixel per point) on white with annotations, as a viewer shows the page.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfReplaceOptions
files.Summary: How writes the new text.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfReplaceResult
files.Summary: What did.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfReplyType
files.Summary: How a markup annotation relates to the one it points at with /IRT (12.5.6.2).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfResetFormAction
files.Summary: A reset-form action (12.7.6.3): returns fields to their default values.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfRevision
files.Summary: One revision of a file (Phase 5 design, 5.1): the original file or one incremental update after it (ISO 32000-2, 7.5.6). Each signature covers one revision; verification opens that revision and compares it with the later ones.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfRevocationSource
files.Summary: Where revocation data (OCSP responses and CRLs) comes from (Phase 5 design Q5): asks each certificate's OCSP responder, then its CRL distribution point, through the caller's ; uses responses the caller already has. Egap never opens a connection on its own.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfRgbColor
files.Summary: A colour in DeviceRGB, each component from 0 to 1, as outline items and annotations give one.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSanitizeOptions
files.Summary: What removes (Phase 5 design Q10); every switch is on by default.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSanitizeResult
files.Summary: What sanitising removed, by kind (Phase 5 design Q10).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSaveMode
files.Summary: How a document is saved.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSaveOptions
files.Summary: Options for saving a document.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSeedValue
files.Summary: A signature field's seed values (/SV, ISO 32000-2, 12.7.5.5): constraints on how the field may be signed, honoured when signing (Phase 5 design Q7).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSeedValueFlags
files.Summary: Which seed values a signer must follow (/Ff of a seed value dictionary, ISO 32000-2, Table 237); a value whose bit is clear is only a suggestion.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSetOcgStateAction
files.Summary: A set-OCG-state action (12.6.4.13): turns optional content groups (layers) on or off.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSignOptions
files.Summary: How a document is signed (Phase 5 design, 5.1).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSignature
files.Summary: A signature or document timestamp in a signed signature field (ISO 32000-2, 12.8): its value dictionary, the bytes it signs and the revision those bytes are. Reading checks nothing cryptographic; reports what is wrong with the byte range itself.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSignatureAppearance
files.Summary: Where and how a signature shows on a page (Phase 5 design Q6). Signatures are invisible unless given one: the layout shows the signer's name with the date, reason and location; lets the caller draw anything with the same as pages. The appearance is part of the signed revision, so it is drawn before the file is hashed.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSignatureChange
files.Summary: One change found in a revision after a signature, with how it is judged and why.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSignatureField
files.Summary: A signature field (12.7.5.5). reads the signatures in signed fields (Phase 5).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSignatureFormat
files.Summary: How the signature value is encoded (/SubFilter, Phase 5 design Q4).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSignatureKind
files.Summary: What a signature is (ISO 32000-2, 12.8).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSignatureReport
files.Summary: What verifying a signature found (Phase 5 design Q8): separate verdicts for integrity, the certificate chain, the timestamp, revocation and the changes made since signing, with the reasons behind each.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSigner
files.Summary: Who signs and with which key (Phase 5 design Q3): a certificate with its private key, or any RSA or ECDsa object with the certificate it belongs to.
