A subclass of RSA or ECDsa reaches a smart card, an HSM or a cloud key service, since Egap only ever asks it to sign the signed attributes. A signature made somewhere else entirely goes through instead.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSquareAnnotation
files.Summary: A square annotation (12.5.6.8): a rectangle drawn inside the annotation's rectangle.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSquigglyAnnotation
files.Summary: A squiggly underline annotation (12.5.6.10, PDF 1.4).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfStamp
files.Summary: A stamp: text, an image or another page drawn on every page (or the pages chosen) as removable page furniture (Phase 7 design 7.3, Q10 and Q11). Make one with , , , or , then set its placement with with.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfStampAnnotation
files.Summary: A rubber stamp annotation (12.5.6.12): a stamp such as Approved or Draft.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfStampResult
files.Summary: What did.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfStampSubtype
files.Summary: The kind of page furniture a stamp is marked as (ISO 32000-2 14.8.2.2, pagination artifacts).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfStream
files.Summary: A PDF stream: a dictionary followed by data. A stream is always an indirect object. Its data stays in the file until it is asked for, and an unchanged stream is copied raw when the file is saved.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfStrikeOutAnnotation
files.Summary: A strikeout annotation (12.5.6.10).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfString
files.Summary: A PDF string: a sequence of bytes, written either as a literal (...) or as hex <...>. A string read from a file keeps its bytes and its form, so an unchanged string writes back the same way.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfStructureElement
files.Summary: An element of the structure tree (ISO 32000-1 14.7.2, Phase 5 design Q14): its type, the text properties assistive technology reads (title, language, alternate, actual and expanded text), attributes and classes, and its children. Changes are written to the element's dictionary at once; the parent tree is rebuilt when the document is saved.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfStructureNode
files.Summary: A child of a structure element (ISO 32000-1 14.7.2): another element, a marked-content sequence or an object.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfStructureTree
files.Summary: A document's logical structure (ISO 32000-1 14.7, Phase 5 design Q14): the tree of structure elements, the role map from the document's own types to standard ones, and the class map of shared attributes. Elements are read from and written to the file's objects directly; the parent tree that leads from page content back to elements is rebuilt from the elements when the document is saved after a change. Page import and merge bring the elements of the pages they copy.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfStructureType
files.Summary: A structure element type (ISO 32000-1 14.8.4, Phase 5 design Q14): one of the standard types, or a document's own type that its role map maps to a standard one. Any name converts to a type.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfSubmitFormAction
files.Summary: A submit-form action (12.7.6.2): sends field values to a URL.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfTextAlignment
files.Summary: How text is aligned in a free text annotation or a field (/Q).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfTextAnnotation
files.Summary: A text annotation (12.5.6.4): a sticky note shown as an icon, its text in a popup.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfTextChange
files.Summary: One change in the text (Phase 7 design Q12).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfTextChangeKind
files.Summary: How a run of words changed.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfTextField
files.Summary: A text field (12.7.5.3): text the user types, on one line or several.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfTextFieldOptions
files.Summary: How a new text field works.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfTextGlyph
files.Summary: One glyph of a page's text (Phase 3 design Q10): the text it stands for, its box in the page's default user space, its font, size and fill colour. A span with /ActualText gives one glyph for the whole span, holding that text.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfTextLine
files.Summary: A line: words on one baseline, in one direction.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfTextMarkupAnnotation
files.Summary: A text markup annotation (12.5.6.10): highlight, underline, squiggly underline or strikeout over text, given as quadrilaterals.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfTextMatch
files.Summary: A run of text found on a page.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfTextOptions
files.Summary: How builds words and lines.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfTextOrder
files.Summary: The order puts text in (Phase 3 design Q10).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfTextPage
files.Summary: A page's text (Phase 3 design Q10): every glyph shown, built into words and lines.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfTextWord
files.Summary: A word: glyphs with no space and no wide gap between them.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfTimestampClient
files.Summary: An RFC 3161 timestamp authority, reached through the caller's (Phase 5 design Q5): Egap never opens a connection on its own and has no default server. The client carries the caller's proxy, timeouts, retries and any credentials the authority wants. Requests are built and responses checked with .NET's .

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfUnderlineAnnotation
files.Summary: An underline annotation (12.5.6.10).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfUriAction
files.Summary: A URI action (12.6.4.8): opens a URI, usually a web address.

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfVerdict
files.Summary: One verdict of a signature report (Phase 5 design Q8).

files.Title: Egap.Pdf.PdfVerifyOptions
files.Summary: Options for verifying a signature (Phase 5 design Q8): the trust anchors are the caller's, there is no built-in trust list, and nothing is fetched from the network unless a revocation source says so.

files.Summary: The XFA form of a document (12.7.8, hub Q7): the form's /XFA, one XDP stream or an array of named packets. Egap keeps it on save as it is, reads its packets, and keeps the datasets packet in step with the AcroForm field values: setting a field's value writes it into the data too. A static XFA form converts to a plain AcroForm with ; a dynamic one, which has no AcroForm fields of its own to fall back on, is reported by and not converted.
